questions.prompt: A lender promises 'no documents, instant money'. What is the best reaction?

options.explanationWrong: Speed and no checks are warning signs, not benefits.

options.text: Treat it as a red flag and check the lender first
Share your ID to speed things up
options.explanationWrong: Never share ID with a lender you have not verified.

options.text: Allow contact access to prove you are real
options.explanationWrong: Contact access can be misused. A loan does not need it.

questions.explanationCorrect: Real lenders check who you are. 'No documents' is a red flag, so check the lender before anything else.

questions.prompt: Why use an interest calculator before borrowing?

options.text: To see only the monthly payment
options.explanationWrong: The monthly payment can hide the total cost.

options.text: To see the total you will repay

options.explanationWrong: A calculator does not change the loan. It shows the cost clearly.
It is one of the best ways to understand a loan.

questions.explanationCorrect: The total repayment is the number that matters. A calculator makes the real cost visible.

options.explanationWrong: App stores are not financial regulators.
A message tells you nothing about who is regulated.

questions.explanationCorrect: RBI regulates lenders and NBFCs. Check a lender through official channels.
